sources.title: On the third secant variety
sources.relevance: Normal-form classification for complex tensors of border rank at most three, used to identify the epsilon-nonzero open part of a four-qutrit third secant.
limitations: The normal-form theorem is stated over the complex numbers.
The source does not state the repository's epsilon characterization; that deduction is proved internally by inspecting the listed normal forms.

repository_usages.assumptions_scope: The imported classification concerns sigma_3 of a Segre product of at least three complex projective factors; the repository applies it to four factors of vector dimension three.
repository_usages.correspondence_note: The four source normal forms are used as an exhaustive case list. The repository separately proves that its cubic epsilon invariant vanishes on types (ii)-(iv) and on sigma_2, while type (i) has nonzero epsilon exactly on the concise GHZ orbit.

sources.title: Equations for the third secant variety of the Segre product of n projective spaces
sources.relevance: Set-theoretic equations for third secants of Segre products, used to make the complete Q-layer boundary trap an exact saturation problem.
limitations: The imported theorem is set-theoretic and does not assert a scheme-theoretic generating set for the secant ideal.
The repository has not yet performed the restricted saturation or produced a radical-membership certificate for its fixed nuisance space.

repository_usages.assumptions_scope: For local vector dimensions at most three, the theorem gives set-theoretic equations for sigma_3 using degree-four Strassen equations for singleton-singleton-rest partitions and 4 x 4 generalized-flattening minors; the repository uses the four-factor, dimension-three case over C.
repository_usages.correspondence_note: The equations are pulled back along the explicit 79-column nuisance map. Their saturation by the pulled-back epsilon invariant is unit exactly when the nuisance space has no epsilon-nonzero third-secant point.
unresolved_obligations: Compute or certify the restricted saturation for the fixed root-torus star nuisance space.
